facts.fact: Ghana's National Identification Authority (NIA) says institutions connected to its verification platform through an API verify customers using Ghana Card numbers.
The NIA says telecommunications companies and some banks verify customers by match-on-card fingerprint checks, and API-connected institutions use the NIA verification platform.

GHA.note: Nothing on who operates or owns the platform beyond NIA's regulatory role.
No public register keyed on the number is named.

facts.fact: The NIA says the existing Ghana Card remains the country's official national identity document, used for transactions requiring identity verification, with fingerprints, iris and face stored on its chip.

systems.platform: chip card with fingerprint, iris and face

facts.fact: The NIA says telecommunications companies and some banks verify customers against the Ghana Card by match-on-card fingerprint checks.
The NIA says both telecommunications companies and some banks use match-on-card verification against the Ghana Card, and API-connected institutions verify by card number.
